decisions.reason: As an innovative but close-to-core display variant, it likely stays because it uses existing cardboard design and production resources and a large firm can tolerate some uncertainty while results remain near aspiration.
This pegboard-back version is somewhat niche, but it is still tightly aligned with the established offer, so management would usually keep it unless performance clearly falls below aspiration.
A standard cardboard quarter-pallet display sits squarely in the firm’s core business, so it is likely to be retained as a baseline offering with low additional organisational strain.
The eighth-pallet format expands retailer choice without requiring a major capability shift, making continued offering likely unless recent sales have been distinctly disappointing.

Because the wooden pallet moves away from the firm’s paper-based core, any performance shortfall versus aspiration is more likely to trigger problemistic search and reallocation back to core display lines.
Although operationally close to the core offer, its focus on media products points to a weaker niche, so management is more likely to drop it if returns have not met aspiration levels.
